title: KCET 2010 Chemistry
subject: chemistry
source: KEA question paper (copy) + KEA answer key column A1

questions.q: In the electrolytic refining of Zinc, .......................
options: the impure metal is at the cathode.
acidified zinc sulphate is the electrolyte.
the metal ion gets reduced at the anode.
questions.chapter: Old syllabus: General Principles and Processes of Isolation of Elements
questions.explanation: In electrorefining, impure Zn is the anode and pure Zn deposits at the cathode (reduction), with acidified ZnSO$_4$ solution as the electrolyte.

questions.q: The wave number of the spectral line in the emission spectrum of hydrogen will be equal to $\dfrac{8}{9}$ times the Rydberg's constant if the electron jumps from .......................
questions.explanation: $\bar\nu = R\left(\dfrac{1}{1^2}-\dfrac{1}{3^2}\right) = R\left(1-\dfrac{1}{9}\right) = \dfrac{8}{9}R$, so the transition is n=3 to n=1.

questions.q:
Consider the following gaseous equilibria with equilibrium constants $K_1$ and $K_2$ respectively.

$SO_{2(g)} + \dfrac{1}{2}O_{2(g)} \rightleftharpoons SO_{3(g)}$

$2SO_{3(g)} \rightleftharpoons 2SO_{2(g)} + O_{2(g)}$

The equilibrium constants are related as .......................
questions.explanation: Reaction 2 is the reverse of reaction 1, doubled: $K_2 = (1/K_1)^2$, so $K_1^2 = 1/K_2$.

questions.q: Enthalpy of vapourization of benzene is +35.3 kJ mol$^{-1}$ at its boiling point of 80$^0$C. The entropy change in the transition of the vapour to liquid at its boiling point [in JK$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$] is ........................
questions.explanation: $\Delta S_{vap} = \dfrac{35300}{353} = 100$ J K$^{-1}$mol$^{-1}$; condensation (vapour to liquid) is the reverse, so $\Delta S = -100$ J K$^{-1}$mol$^{-1}$.

questions.q: Which one of the following conversions involve change in both hybridization and shape?
questions.explanation: BF$_3$ is sp$^2$ hybridized and trigonal planar, while BF$_4^-$ is sp$^3$ hybridized and tetrahedral, changing both hybridization and shape.

questions.q: In chromite ore, the oxidation number of iron and chromium are respectively ...............
questions.explanation: Chromite ore is FeCr$_2$O$_4$; balancing charges with O at -2 gives Fe as +2 and Cr as +3.

questions.q:
For the reversible reaction

$A_{(s)} + B_{(g)} \rightleftharpoons C_{(g)} + D_{(g)}$ : $\Delta G^0 = -350\ kJ$.

Which one of the following statements is true?
options: Equilibrium constant is greater than one.
The reaction is thermodynamically not feasible.
questions.explanation: Since $\Delta G^0 = -RT\ln K$ is large and negative, $K \gg 1$, i.e. the equilibrium constant is greater than one.

questions.q:
Out of the below two compounds, the vapour pressure of (B) at a particular temperature is ...............

[(A) = para-nitrophenol: a benzene ring with $-$OH and $-$NO$_2$ groups para to each other; (B) = ortho-nitrophenol: a benzene ring with $-$OH and $-$NO$_2$ groups ortho to each other]
options: higher or lower than (A), depending on the size of the vessel.
questions.explanation: Ortho-nitrophenol (B) has intramolecular hydrogen bonding, reducing intermolecular association, so it is more volatile and has a higher vapour pressure than the para isomer (A), which has intermolecular H-bonding.

questions.q: The amount of heat evolved when 500 cm$^3$ of 0.1 M $HCl$ is mixed with 200 cm$^3$ of 0.2 M $NaOH$ is .......................
questions.explanation: Moles HCl = 0.05, moles NaOH = 0.04 (limiting). Heat evolved = 0.04 mol $\times$ 57.3 kJ/mol $\approx$ 2.292 kJ.

questions.q: During the adsorption of krypton on activated charcoal at low temperature, ...............
questions.explanation: Adsorption is exothermic ($\Delta H < 0$) and randomness decreases as gas molecules get confined on the surface ($\Delta S < 0$).

questions.q: The set of quantum numbers for the outermost electron for copper in its ground state is.......................
questions.explanation: Cu is [Ar]3d$^{10}$4s$^1$; the outermost electron is in 4s, giving n=4, l=0, m=0, s=+1/2.

questions.q:
Peroxide ion .......................
a) is diamagnetic.
b) has five completely filled antibonding molecular orbitals.
c) is isoelectronic with neon.
d) has bond order one.
Which one of these is correct?
questions.explanation: O$_2^{2-}$ has all electrons paired (diamagnetic) and bond order 1 (8 bonding, 6 antibonding valence electrons); it is isoelectronic with F$_2$ (not Ne) and has only 3 filled antibonding MOs, so only (a) and (d) are correct.

questions.q: Which one of these is NOT true for benzene?
options: There are three carbon-carbon single bonds and three carbon-carbon double bonds.
It forms only one type of monosubstituted product.
The bond angle between the carbon-carbon bonds is 120$^0$.
The heat of hydrogenation of benzene is less than the theoretical value.
questions.explanation: Due to resonance/delocalization all six C-C bonds in benzene are equivalent (bond order 1.5), so describing three fixed single and three fixed double bonds is not true.

questions.q: A mixture of $CaCl_2$ and $NaCl$ weighing 4.44 g is treated with sodium carbonate solution to precipitate all the $Ca^{+2}$ ions as calcium carbonate. The calcium carbonate so obtained is heated strongly to get 0.56 g of $CaO$. The percentage of $NaCl$ in the mixture (atomic mass of $Ca$ = 40) is ...............
questions.explanation: Moles CaO = 0.56/56 = 0.01 = moles Ca, mass Ca = 0.4 g, mass CaCl$_2$ = 0.01 $\times$ 111 = 1.11 g, so NaCl = 4.44 - 1.11 = 3.33 g, i.e. 75%.

questions.q: For one mole of an ideal gas, increasing the temperature from 10$^0$C to 20$^0$C ...............
options: increases the rms velocity by $\sqrt{2}$ times.
increases the average kinetic energy by two times.
increases both the average kinetic energy and rms velocity, but not significantly.
increases the rms velocity by two times.
questions.explanation: T changes from 283 K to 293 K, only a ~3.5% rise, so both average KE ($\propto T$) and rms velocity ($\propto \sqrt{T}$) increase only slightly, not by a factor of 2 or $\sqrt{2}$.

questions.q: Generally, the first ionization energy increases along a period. But there are some exceptions. One which is NOT an exception is ...............
questions.explanation: Be-B, N-O and Mg-Al are known exceptions (due to stable filled/half-filled subshells); Na to Mg follows the normal increasing trend.

questions.q: 50 cm$^3$ of 0.2 N $HCl$ is titrated against 0.1 N $NaOH$ solution. The titration is discontinued after adding 50 cm$^3$ of $NaOH$. The remaining titration is completed by adding 0.5 N $KOH$. The volume of $KOH$ required for completing the titration is ...............
questions.explanation: Milli-equivalents of HCl = 10; NaOH added = 5; remaining HCl = 5 meq, needing 5/0.5 = 10 cm$^3$ of 0.5 N KOH.

questions.q: In which one of the following, does the given amount of chlorine exert the least pressure in a vessel of capacity 1 dm$^3$ at 273K?
questions.explanation: 0.0355 g Cl$_2$ = 0.0005 mol, the smallest number of moles among the options, so it exerts the least pressure (pressure is proportional to moles at fixed V, T).

questions.q: Based on the first law of thermodynamics, which one of the following is correct?
questions.explanation: Using $\Delta U = q + w$, for a cyclic process $\Delta U = 0$, so $q = -w$.

questions.q: For alkali metals, which one of the following trends is INCORRECT?
options: Ionization energy : Li > Na > K > Rb
Hydration energy : Li > Na > K > Rb
Atomic size : Li < Na < K < Rb
questions.explanation: Density does not increase smoothly down the group; potassium is actually less dense than sodium, so 'Li < Na < K < Rb' is incorrect.

questions.q: One gram of silver gets distributed between 10 cm$^3$ of molten zinc and 100 cm$^3$ of molten lead at 800$^0$C. The percentage of silver in the zinc layer is approximately ...............
questions.chapter: Old syllabus: General Principles and Processes of Isolation of Elements
questions.explanation: In the Parkes process, the distribution coefficient of Ag between molten Zn and Pb is about 300, i.e. $\dfrac{x/10}{(1-x)/100}=300$ where $x$ is the mass of Ag (in g) in the zinc layer; solving gives $x\approx0.97$, so despite its much smaller volume, the zinc layer ends up with about 97% of the silver.

questions.q: One mole of an organic compound 'A' with the formula $C_3H_8O$ reacts completely with two moles of $HI$ to form X and Y. When 'Y' is boiled with aqueous alkali forms Z. Z answers the iodoform test. The compound 'A' is ...............
questions.explanation: Methoxyethane (CH$_3$OC$_2$H$_5$) is cleaved by excess HI to CH$_3$I (X) and C$_2$H_5I (Y); Y hydrolysed with alkali gives ethanol (Z), which gives a positive iodoform test.

questions.q: The IUPAC name of $K_2[Ni(CN)_4]$ is ...............
questions.explanation: The complex ion is $[Ni(CN)_4]^{2-}$ with Ni in +2 state; cyano ligands (CN$^-$) named 'cyano', giving potassium tetracyanonickelate(II).

questions.q: The spin only magnetic moment of $Mn^{+4}$ ion is nearly ...................
questions.explanation: Mn$^{4+}$ has configuration 3d$^3$ (3 unpaired electrons); $\mu = \sqrt{3(3+2)} = \sqrt{15} \approx 3.87 \approx 4$ BM.

questions.q: In Kjeldahl's method, ammonia from 5 g of food neutralizes 30 cm$^3$ of 0.1 N acid. The percentage of nitrogen in the food is ............................
questions.chapter: Organic Chemistry: Basic Principles and Techniques
questions.explanation: %N = $\dfrac{1.4 \times N \times V}{W} = \dfrac{1.4 \times 0.1 \times 30}{5} = 0.84$.

questions.q: Carbon can reduce ferric oxide to iron at a temperature above 983 K because ...............
options: carbon has a higher affinity towards oxidation than iron.
carbon monoxide formed is thermodynamically less stable than ferric oxide.
iron has a higher affinity towards oxygen than carbon.
free energy change for the formation of carbon dioxide is less negative than that for ferric oxide.
questions.chapter: Old syllabus: General Principles and Processes of Isolation of Elements
questions.explanation: On the Ellingham diagram, the C/CO line crosses below the Fe/Fe$_2$O$_3$ line above ~983 K, meaning carbon then has a greater affinity for oxygen than iron and can reduce its oxide.

questions.q: An oxygen containing organic compound upon oxidation forms a carboxylic acid as the only organic product with its molecular mass higher by 14 units. The organic compound is...............
questions.explanation: Oxidation of RCH$_2$OH (primary alcohol) to RCOOH adds one O and removes two H, a net mass increase of +14; oxidation of an aldehyde would only add O (+16).

questions.q: The compound obtained when acetaldehyde reacts with dilute aqueous sodium hydroxide exhibits ...............
questions.explanation: Aldol condensation gives 3-hydroxybutanal, CH$_3$CH(OH)CH$_2$CHO, which has one chiral carbon and hence shows optical isomerism, but no C=C stereocentre for geometric isomerism.

questions.q: The activation energy for a reaction at the temperature TK was found to be 2.303 RT J mol$^{-1}$. The ratio of the rate constant to Arrhenius factor is ...............
A dibromo derivative of an alkane reacts with sodium metal to form an alicyclic hydrocarbon. The derivative is ...............
questions.explanation: 1,4-dibromobutane undergoes intramolecular Wurtz (Freund) reaction with Na to give cyclobutane, an alicyclic hydrocarbon.

questions.q: Time required for 100 percent completion of a zero order reaction is ...............
questions.explanation: For a zero order reaction, $kt = x$; complete reaction means $x = a$, so $t = a/k$.

questions.q: 0.023 g of sodium metal is reacted with 100 cm$^3$ of water. The pH of the resulting solution is ...................
questions.explanation: Moles Na = 0.023/23 = 0.001 giving 0.001 mol NaOH in 0.1 L, so [OH$^-$] = 0.01 M, pOH = 2, pH = 12.

questions.q: Which one of the following is wrongly matched?
questions.explanation: CN$^-$ is a strong field ligand, so $[Fe(CN)_6]^{3-}$ is low spin with $d^2sp^3$ hybridization, not $sp^3d^2$ (which is used for weak-field, high-spin octahedral complexes).

questions.q: Which one of the following conformations of cyclohexane is the least stable?
questions.explanation: The half-chair conformation has the highest torsional and steric strain among cyclohexane conformations, making it the least stable.

questions.q: Which one of the following is a molecular crystal?
questions.explanation: Dry ice (solid CO$_2$) is held together by weak van der Waals forces between discrete molecules, making it a molecular crystal.

questions.q: A buffer solution contains 0.1 mole of sodium acetate dissolved in 1000 cm$^3$ of 0.1 M acetic acid. To the above buffer solution, 0.1 mole of sodium acetate is further added and dissolved. The pH of the resulting buffer is equal to ...............
questions.explanation: After addition, salt = 0.2 mol, acid = 0.1 mol; $pH = pK_a + \log(0.2/0.1) = pK_a + \log 2$.

questions.q: Which one of the following has the most nucleophilic nitrogen?
questions.explanation: In pyrrole and aniline the nitrogen lone pair is delocalized into the aromatic ring, and in acetanilide it is further delocalized into the carbonyl, but in pyridine the lone pair sits in an sp$^2$ orbital outside the aromatic system, making it most nucleophilic.

questions.q: Chloroacetic acid is a stronger acid than acetic acid. This can be explained using .........
questions.explanation: The electronegative chlorine withdraws electron density inductively (-I effect), stabilizing the conjugate base and increasing acidity.

questions.q: The correct sequence of reactions to convert p-nitrophenol into quinol involves ...........
questions.explanation: p-Nitrophenol is reduced to p-aminophenol, diazotized to the diazonium salt, then hydrolysed to give quinol (hydroquinone).

questions.q: $CH_3CH_2Br \xrightarrow[\Delta]{Aq\ KOH} A \xrightarrow[\Delta]{KMnO_4/H^+} B \xrightarrow[\Delta]{NH_3} C \xrightarrow[alkali]{Br_2} D$ ; "D" is ...............
questions.explanation: A = ethanol, B = acetic acid, C = acetamide (CH$_3$CONH$_2$); Hofmann bromamide degradation of C with Br$_2$/alkali gives D = methylamine, CH$_3$NH$_2$.

questions.q: The letter 'D' in D-glucose signifies ...............
options: configuration at a particular chiral carbon
questions.explanation: The D/L label refers only to the configuration at the reference chiral carbon (the highest-numbered/penultimate carbon), compared to glyceraldehyde, not to optical rotation.

questions.q: Reaction of methyl bromide with aqueous sodium hydroxide involves ...................
questions.explanation: Methyl bromide is a primary halide with no steric hindrance and reacts with a strong nucleophile (OH$^-$) via the bimolecular $S_N2$ mechanism.

questions.q: 9.65 C of electric current is passed through fused anhydrous magnesium chloride. The magnesium metal thus obtained is completely converted into a Grignard reagent. The number of moles of the Grignard reagent obtained is ...............
questions.explanation: Moles of electrons = 9.65/96500 = $10^{-4}$; Mg$^{2+}$ + 2e$^-$ $\rightarrow$ Mg gives moles Mg = $5\times10^{-5}$, and Mg + RX $\rightarrow$ RMgX is 1:1, so moles Grignard reagent = $5\times10^{-5}$.

questions.q: Which one of the following does NOT involve coagulation?
options: Clotting of blood by the use of ferric chloride
Treatment of drinking water by potash alum
questions.explanation: Peptization is the reverse of coagulation — it converts a freshly precipitated solid back into a colloidal sol; the other options are all examples of coagulation.

questions.q: In alkaline medium, alanine exists predominantly as/in ...............
questions.explanation: In alkaline medium the carboxylate retains its negative charge while the amino group is deprotonated (not protonated), so the amino acid exists predominantly as the anion.

questions.q: The standard emf of a galvanic cell involving 3 moles of electrons in its redox reaction is 0.59 V. The equilibrium constant for the reaction of the cell is ...................
Benzaldehyde and acetone can be best distinguished using ...............
questions.explanation: Tollens' reagent gives a silver mirror with benzaldehyde (an aldehyde) but not with acetone (a ketone); Fehling's solution and 2,4-DNPH do not distinguish them (aromatic aldehydes don't reduce Fehling's, and both give a 2,4-DNPH precipitate).

questions.q: Which one of the following statements is true?
options: Saponification of oil yields a diol
Addition of antioxidant to oil minimizes rancidity
questions.explanation: Antioxidants inhibit the autoxidation of fats/oils, preventing oxidative rancidity; saponification actually yields glycerol (a triol) plus soap, and drying oils undergo oxidative polymerization, not hydrolysis.

questions.q:
The following data is obtained during the first order thermal decomposition of $2A_{(g)} \longrightarrow B_{(g)} + C_{(s)}$, at constant volume and temperature.

[Table: At the end of 10 minutes, total pressure = 300 Pa; After completion, total pressure = 200 Pa]

The rate constant in min$^{-1}$ is ...............
questions.explanation: Total pressure at completion = $P_0/2 = 200$ Pa, so $P_0 = 400$ Pa; at t=10 min, pressure of A left = $2(P_0 - 300) = 200$ Pa. $k = \dfrac{2.303}{10}\log\dfrac{400}{200} = 0.0693\ min^{-1}$.

questions.q: Phenol $\xrightarrow{X}$ forms a tribromo derivative. "X" is ...............
questions.explanation: Phenol reacts readily with bromine water (aqueous Br$_2$) to give the white precipitate of 2,4,6-tribromophenol, due to the strong activating effect of -OH.

questions.q: The correct sequence of steps involved in the mechanism of Cannizzaro's reaction is .......
options: transfer of $H^-$, transfer of $H^+$ and nucleophilic attack
nucleophilic attack, transfer of $H^-$ and transfer of $H^+$
electrophilic attack by $OH^-$, transfer of $H^+$ and transfer of $H^-$
transfer of $H^+$, nucleophilic attack and transfer of $H^-$
questions.explanation: OH$^-$ first adds (nucleophilic attack) to one aldehyde molecule, the resulting intermediate transfers a hydride (H$^-$) to a second aldehyde molecule, and finally a proton (H$^+$) is transferred to give the alcohol and carboxylate.

questions.q: Which one of the following is an example for homogeneous catalysis?
options: Manufacture of ammonia by Haber's process
Manufacture of sulphuric acid by contact process
Hydrolysis of sucrose in presence of dilute hydrochloric acid
questions.explanation: In acid hydrolysis of sucrose, the HCl catalyst and the sucrose solution are in the same (liquid) phase, making it homogeneous catalysis, unlike the other options which use solid catalysts with gaseous/liquid reactants.

questions.q: The empirical formula of a nonelectrolyte is $C_1H_2O_1$. A solution containing 6 g of the compound exerts the same osmotic pressure as that of 0.05 M glucose solution at the same temperature. The molecular formula of the compound is ...............
questions.explanation: Equal osmotic pressure at the same temperature means equal molar concentration (0.05 M); for 6 g in 1 L this gives a molar mass of 120 g/mol, i.e. $(CH_2O)_4 = C_4H_8O_4$.

questions.q: A white crystalline salt A reacts with dilute $HCl$ to liberate a suffocating gas B and also forms a yellow precipitate. The gas B turns potassium dichromate acidified with dilute $H_2SO_4$ to a green coloured solution C. A, B and C are respectively ...................
questions.explanation: Sodium thiosulfate with dilute HCl disproportionates to give sulfur (yellow precipitate) and SO$_2$ gas (suffocating), which reduces acidified orange K$_2$Cr$_2$O$_7$ to green Cr$_2$(SO$_4$)$_3$.

questions.q: Molecules of a noble gas do not possess vibrational energy because a noble gas .............
questions.explanation: Vibrational energy requires at least two bonded atoms; noble gases exist as single, monoatomic molecules with no bonds to vibrate.

questions.q:
One dm$^3$ solution containing $10^{-5}$ moles each of $Cl^-$ ions and $CrO_4^{-2}$ ions is treated with $10^{-4}$ mole of silver nitrate. Which one of the following observations is made?

$[K_{SP}\ Ag_2CrO_4 = 4\times10^{-12}]$

$[K_{SP}\ AgCl = 1\times10^{-10}]$
options: Both silver chromate and silver chloride start precipitating simultaneously.
questions.explanation: AgCl requires a much lower [Ag$^+$] to reach its $K_{sp}$ (10$^{-10}$/10$^{-5}$ = 10$^{-5}$ M) than Ag$_2$CrO$_4$ (needs $\sqrt{4\times10^{-12}/10^{-5}} \approx 2\times10^{-4}$ M), so AgCl precipitates first as Ag$^+$ is added.

questions.q: pH value of which one of the following is not equal to one?
options: 50 cm$^3$ of 0.4 M $HCl$ + 50 cm$^3$ of 0.2 M $NaOH$
questions.explanation: 0.1 M CH$_3$COOH is a weak acid, only partially ionized, so its pH is greater than 1, unlike the other three which all give [H$^+$] = 0.1 M (pH = 1).

questions.q:
$E_1$, $E_2$ and $E_3$ are the emf values of the three galvanic cells respectively.

a) $Zn | Zn^{+2}_{1M} || Cu^{+2}_{0.1M} | Cu$

b) $Zn | Zn^{+2}_{1M} || Cu^{+2}_{1M} | Cu$

c) $Zn | Zn^{+2}_{0.1M} || Cu^{+2}_{1M} | Cu$

Which one of the following is true?
questions.explanation: By the Nernst equation, $E=E^\circ-\dfrac{0.0591}{2}\log\dfrac{[Zn^{2+}]}{[Cu^{2+}]}$, so increasing $[Cu^{2+}]$ or decreasing $[Zn^{2+}]$ raises the emf: cell (c) (low Zn$^{2+}$, high Cu$^{2+}$) has the highest emf and cell (a) (low Cu$^{2+}$) the lowest, giving $E_3 > E_2 > E_1$.

questions.q: The IUPAC name of [CH$_3$CH$_2$-CHBr-CH(CH$_3$)-CHO, drawn as a skeletal structure with CHO at one end, a methyl branch at C2 and Br at C3] is ......................
questions.explanation: The longest chain including the CHO carbon has 5 carbons (pentanal) with a methyl at C2 and Br at C3, giving 3-bromo-2-methylpentanal.

questions.q: Which one of the following forms propanenitrile as the major product?
questions.explanation: Alcoholic KCN reacts via the nucleophilic cyanide carbon (C-attack) with ethyl bromide to give ethyl cyanide (propanenitrile, CH$_3$CH$_2$CN); AgCN, being covalent, favours N-attack to give isocyanides instead.
